sixppac-bit-encoding.alt: The circuit stores −1 as 0 (LO) and +1 as 1 (HI). A match gives XNOR 1 and product +1. A mismatch gives XNOR 0 and product −1. Summing over N positions yields the same dot product as corrected AND products.
sixppac-bit-encoding.caption: The 0/1 circuit codes represent −1/+1. Matching bits contribute +1, and differing bits contribute −1.

sixppac-four-bit-walkthrough.alt: For b=(1,0,1,1) and c=(1,1,0,1), positions one and four match, giving 2×2−4=0. The AND sum is 2 and each vector has three ones, so 4×2−2×3−2×3+4=0. Changing the last c bit to 0 gives −2 on both paths. These are illustrative values.
sixppac-four-bit-walkthrough.caption: An invented four-bit input shows position by position why XNOR match counts and corrected AND sums yield the same bipolar dot product.
